"HAUNTED TOWN: THE LAST ESCAPE

Complete 3D Survival Horror Game

Create a fully playable, realistic 3D open-world survival horror game.

GAME STYLE

- Genre: Survival horror, adventure, exploration, mystery.
- Graphics: Photorealistic 3D, Unreal Engine 5 quality.
- Camera: First-person perspective.
- Environment: Modern abandoned town, haunted houses, forests, garages and roads.
- Time: Mostly nighttime, with fog, rain and thunderstorms.
- Sound: Realistic footsteps, breathing, ghost whispers, doors, wind and atmospheric horror music.
- Main gameplay: Exploration, escaping ghosts, rescuing friends, solving puzzles, collecting car parts and repairing a vehicle.

STORY

The main character wakes up at 2:30 AM inside his haunted house.

The electricity is unstable. Doors open automatically. Strange sounds come from upstairs. A ghost is wandering through the house.

The main entrance is locked.

The player must find the keys, restore electricity and escape through the back entrance.

Outside, the player discovers that three friends are hiding in different parts of the town.

The four friends must work together to escape the haunted town.

CHARACTERS

Create four playable-story characters:

1. Main character: Player controlled.
2. Alex: Mechanic who can repair vehicles.
3. Sam: Good at finding hidden objects.
4. Mike: Strong character who can move heavy objects.

Friends should follow the player, react to danger and help with missions.

OPEN-WORLD MAP

Create a connected, explorable town containing:

- Haunted residential house.
- Abandoned supermarket.
- Mechanic garage.
- Petrol station.
- Police station.
- Hospital.
- Abandoned factory.
- Forest.
- Main road.
- Town exit and bridge.

Every location must have interactive objects and useful items.

HORROR AI

Create four types of ghosts:

1. Stalker: Follows the player from a distance.
2. Screamer: Appears suddenly.
3. Hunter: Detects footsteps and chases the player.
4. House Ghost: Protects the haunted house.

Ghost AI must include patrol, searching, chasing, attacking and losing sight of the player.

The player must be able to hide under beds, inside cupboards and behind objects.

MAIN OBJECTIVE

The main objective is to repair an abandoned car and escape the town.

Required items:

- Engine.
- Car battery.
- Four tyres.
- Fuel tank.
- Car key.
- Spark plugs.
- Radiator.
- Electrical wiring.

Create individual missions to locate every part.

Allow the player to carry items, place them in inventory, transport them and physically install them in the car.

CAR MECHANICS

Create realistic vehicle gameplay:

- Car doors that open.
- Bonnet that opens.
- Engine installation.
- Tyre installation.
- Battery and wiring connection.
- Fuel system.
- Ignition system.
- Engine starting animation.
- Realistic driving and steering.
- Headlights and horn.
- Fuel consumption and vehicle damage.

The car must not start until all mandatory components are installed and the ignition key is obtained.

SURVIVAL SYSTEM

Include:

- Flashlight with battery consumption.
- Health.
- Stamina.
- Inventory.
- Hiding.
- Sound detection.
- Limited resources.
- Safe rooms.
- Save checkpoints.

MISSIONS

Create a complete mission system with:

- Main missions.
- Optional side missions.
- Search missions.
- Rescue missions.
- Puzzle missions.
- Vehicle repair missions.

Show mission objectives on screen and reward completed missions with useful items.

FINAL MISSION

Once the car is repaired, all four friends must enter the vehicle.

The player drives through the haunted town while ghosts chase the car.

The player must avoid obstacles, drive through the forest and reach the town exit.

Finish with a cinematic escape scene.

After the escape, the car radio switches on automatically and a mysterious voice says:

\"You forgot someone.\"

End the game with a mysterious sequel teaser.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

- Fully playable 3D game, not just a cinematic.
- Functional player movement and camera.
- Functional NPC companions.
- Working ghost AI.
- Interactive objects.
- Working inventory.
- Functional mission progression.
- Functional car assembly.
- Working vehicle physics.
- Realistic environmental audio.
- Proper collision and navigation.
- Autosave and checkpoints.
- Main menu, pause menu and settings.
- Optimized graphics and performance.

Build the game in development stages. First create a playable haunted house, then companions, town exploration, ghost AI, missions, vehicle assembly and finally the escape sequence.

Prioritize functional gameplay over decorative graphics. Do not leave mission objectives or essential interactions as nonfunctional placeholders.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build “HAUNTED TOWN: THE LAST ESCAPE” as a playable browser-based 3D survival horror game in the existing project.

## Requirements
- First-person exploration, haunted house opening, connected town, ghosts, companions, inventory and survival, scavenging and car assembly, then a playable escape sequence.
- Prioritize functional gameplay; do not ask clarifying questions. Save small JPEG screenshots for checks and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone Three.js browser game, with no build framework added.
- Used procedural geometry and simple lighting/materials instead of external assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a designed title/menu and HUD, plus initial Three.js scene content: haunted house, town buildings, road, forest, bridge, rain, objects, and a sedan.
- Added partial gameplay data and interactions for house escape, friends, parts, ghosts, vehicle repair, missions, and checkpoint saving.

### Active
- `game.js` is incomplete and has not been verified; core game loop, input/UI event wiring, collision/movement, interaction targeting, ghost behavior, driving, and ending still need implementation.
- No browser run or screenshot verification has occurred.

### Blocked
- Current game is not yet runnable as a complete playable experience; `loadCheckpoint()` references `hk`, but the house-key variable is named `houseKey`.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `game.js` from its current end and fix broken references/logic, including `hk` versus `houseKey` and pickup relocation/glow updates.
2. Finish player movement, mouse/touch controls, interaction selection, HUD/menu/pause/journal events, audio feedback, ghost AI, companion following, and car driving/escape logic.
3. Run the project and resolve JavaScript/runtime errors.
4. Capture and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot; report the tested scope and any remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, menus, CSS, Three.js import map, and `game.js` entry point.
- `game.js`: In-progress procedural scene and gameplay implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `game.js` currently ends at `loadCheckpoint()`; there is no animation/game loop or event-handler setup yet.
